defiant-nadia.title: Defiant Nadia
defiant-nadia.subject_description: Strongly presumed to be a biopic of Mary Ann Evans (1908-1996), the Australian-born stunt actress known as 'Fearless Nadia.' Born in Perth to a British soldier and a Greek mother, she moved to India in 1928, joined Wadia Movietone under producer J.B.H. Wadia, and became the first female action star of Indian cinema with 'Hunterwali' (1935). Famous for cracking a bullwhip, masked stunts, and riding her horse Punjab-Ka-Beta across 1930s-40s Hindi cinema. No prior public announcement ties Alliance Productions India or Deepak Tijori to a Fearless Nadia project; previous biopic attempts attached to Shekhar Kapur, Vishal Bharadwaj and Sohail Khan have all stalled.
defiant-nadia.elevator_2_sentences: A defiant Australian woman reinvents herself in 1930s Bombay and becomes Hunterwali, the masked, whip-cracking stunt heroine who electrified pre-Independence India and quietly built the template for every female action star that followed. Defiant Nadia is a globe-spanning, English-Hindi-language origin story of cinema's original action queen, a Wadia-era spectacle pitched at prestige streamers seeking the next 'The Crown'-scale female biopic from the subcontinent.
defiant-nadia.notes: No press footprint yet for 'Defiant Nadia' as a titled project. Subject identification is high-confidence (no other notable 'Nadia' fits 'defiant') but the Alliance / Tijori attachment is unconfirmed in public sources. Treat the website teaser as a soft reveal; recommend cross-checking the title with the director before publishing.

kabuliwala.title: Kabuliwala
kabuliwala.subject_description: Feature adaptation of Rabindranath Tagore's 1892 Bengali short story 'Kabuliwala' ('The Man from Kabul'), about a Pashtun dry-fruit vendor in Calcutta who befriends a small Bengali girl who reminds him of the daughter he left in Afghanistan. Directed by Goncourt Prize-winning Afghan-French author-filmmaker Atiq Rahimi (Earth and Ashes, The Patience Stone / Syngue Sabour). Screenplay by the late Jean-Claude Carriere (Bunuel's long-time collaborator, d. 2021), Atiq Rahimi and Rosemary Ricchio. Music by Eric Neveux, cinematography by Reynald Capurro, edited by Francoise Tournier, production design by Eve Martin. Indian producer of record on the long-gestating package is Mumbai-based Sunil Doshi; Alliance Productions India's involvement (and Deepak Tijori's on-screen role as the Pashtun vendor Rahmat) appears to be a 2025-26 revival of a project Rahimi and Carriere first developed in 2005-07.
kabuliwala.status: Pre-production / financing close (poster carries 'Festival de Cannes Official Selection' branding; Cannes 2025 official lineup did not list it under that title, so this may be a Marche du Film / market-stage promo asset rather than an in-competition confirmation - verify before publishing the Cannes claim)
kabuliwala.alliance_role: Co-producer and lead-actor vehicle (Deepak Tijori as Rahmat the Kabuliwala)
kabuliwala.elevator_2_sentences: From Goncourt laureate Atiq Rahimi and the late Jean-Claude Carriere comes a luminous, border-crossing reimagining of Tagore's most beloved short story: a Pashtun fruit-seller exiled in Kolkata finds a daughter in a Bengali child, and a country in a stranger. A stranger, a child, a bond beyond borders - festival-grade arthouse with built-in awards pedigree and a natural home at A24, MUBI or Netflix's prestige world-cinema slate.
kabuliwala.notes: Important context: Rahimi's March 2026 novel 'Kabuliwalla, c'est moi' (P.O.L.) is explicitly autobiographical about the failed 2005-07 film attempt - so the film version going to Cannes/markets in 2025-26 would be a revival, presumably with Alliance Productions India stepping in alongside or in place of Sunil Doshi. The Carriere screenplay credit is posthumous (he died Feb 2021). Recommend the website say 'Festival de Cannes - Marche du Film 2025' rather than 'Official Selection' unless the director can produce the official festival listing.

khoj.title: Khoj
khoj.subject_description: Hindi word for 'search' / 'investigation' / 'quest.' No publicly announced Alliance Productions India, Deepak Tijori or Mandeep Kaur Tijori project under this title surfaces in trade press, IMDb (the only 'Khoj' listings are the 1989 Aruna Raje thriller and an unrelated 2017 short), or social channels as of May 2026. Likely a confidential development title - working title, internal slate name, or a script in pre-development.
khoj.elevator_2_sentences: Khoj - 'the search' - is Alliance Productions India's confidential next Hindi-language original, a contemporary domestic story in development for 2026-27. Further details will be unveiled at the project's official announcement.
khoj.notes: Nothing publicly findable. Use a placeholder teaser card with 'Title TBA / In Development' framing. Ask the director for one logline + genre + market (national vs international) before going live - even a single sentence will let the card avoid feeling thinner than the other two.
